chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbat, from the one who mentioned him, from Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام), who said:
So I said to Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام), "Is poverty from the dinar and the dirham?" He said, "No, but from the religion."

key_terms.الدِّرْهَمِ: dirham; a silver coin representing monetary possessions
key_terms.الدِّينَارِ: dinar; a gold coin representing material wealth
key_terms.الدِّينِ: religion; here, faith and religious commitment whose loss is the true poverty
key_terms.الْفَقْرُ: poverty; here, a state of deprivation whose deeper meaning is clarified as spiritual rather than financial
key_terms.الْمَوْتُ الْأَحْمَرُ: the red death; an intense expression for a grave and devastating affliction

ai.seo_question: What does Imam Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام) mean by saying that poverty is from religion, not from dinars and dirhams?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that the most dangerous form of poverty is not lack of money, but lack of religion. It shifts attention from material deprivation to spiritual loss, presenting religious impoverishment as a far more severe calamity.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Asbat, from the one who mentioned it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
So I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘(Is it) the poverty from the Dinars and the Dirhams?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, but from the Religion’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Asbat from those he has mentioned (in his book) from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘
I (the narrator) then asked him, ‘Is it poverty due to deficiency of Dirham and Dinar (units of money)?’ The Imam said, ‘No, in fact, it is poverty due to deficiency in religion.’”
